narrative.overview:
Open Color Picker is a compact Rust/GTK3 color reference for the Linux desktop. Native controls provide familiar actions and feedback; the selected color and discrete pixel magnifier supply the visual identity.

The desktop theme owns the surrounding interface. App-owned drawing stays factual: solid color samples, readable numeric values, and a precise indication of the selected source pixel.
keyCharacteristics: GTK3 controls that follow the desktop's light or dark theme.
Monospace color values beside ordinary system labels.
Solid sampled-color surfaces and a discrete source-pixel magnifier.

rules.name: The Theme Ownership Rule
rules.body: Keep application chrome, action accents, error treatment, focus states, borders, and control shapes under GTK's theme. A selected or default sample is color data, not a brand token.

rules.name: The Source Pixel Rule
rules.body: Show and sample original captured pixels. Use nearest-neighbor scaling for the captured image and solid cells for magnification; never derive a selected value from an interpolated display pixel.

rules.name: The Native Type Rule
rules.body: Inherit the desktop's interface typography for labels, help, status, and header bars. Apply the recorded monospace roles only to numeric color information.

rules.name: The Native Depth Rule
rules.body: Let GTK and the window manager supply control and window elevation. The app's Cairo swatch and magnifier have no added shadow.

dos: Do preserve GTK's suggested actions, symbolic icons, focus treatment, and light/dark theme behavior.
Do pair sampled color with a readable value and an accessible name.
Do preserve native button activation when focus leaves the picker canvas.
Do keep errors and empty states written, visible, and actionable.
donts: Don't turn a sampled color or a screenshot's theme colors into fixed application chrome.
Don't smooth source pixels in the picker or magnifier.
Don't replace GTK controls with a custom web-style control system.
